findings.summary: the bump's own contract gap was guarded with a third hand-written inventory METHOD, in a file whose other two contract kinds are static tables driven by one loop (`shapeContracts`, `orderContracts`) -- so each further guarded body would have cost a method, a hand-added call and a third copy of the projection lambda. It is now `inventoryContracts`, one `[symbol, restated, kinds]` row per body, which also makes the set of guarded bodies read beside the set of restated ones

the real hole the bump exposed was wider than the statement it added: `createPhysicsAggregate`, `createPhysicsBody` and `setPhysicsShapeMaterial` are restated whole by the same emitted translation unit under presence-only contracts, and `orderContracts` walks with a cursor that skips anything inserted BETWEEN two ordered calls -- so the line 1.26.0 added to `setPhysicsBodyMass` would have been equally silent in any of them. Upstream added that identical line to two pinned functions and the port was faithful only because the second is unlowered. All three now carry inventory rows, `createPhysicsAggregate` (10 statements) being the one the aggregate restates end to end

`STATEMENT_KINDS` had no `return statement` entry, so the returns closing `createPhysicsAggregate` and `createPhysicsBody` projected as `"other statement"` -- an inventory that cannot name a kind it contains is one a real change can slip through. Added

the statement-kind projection was copy-pasted verbatim between the two inventory callers, stating the `"other statement"` fallback the refusal message prints twice; it is one module-level `statementKind` beside the table now, so the two cannot disagree about a kind the table has no entry for

`assertInventory`'s own doc said "Two bodies here are restated whole" and enumerated two callers; the new row set makes it five bodies across two projections. Generalised rather than re-counted, so the next row does not invalidate it again

the new method's doc restated, for the third time in the file and the fourth counting `assertInventory`'s own error text, the generic "an added arm is invisible to a per-expression check" rationale. The version-specific observation is the only part that was new, so it moved to the table's header and the per-statement facts stayed in the row comments, where they cannot drift from the array

no writer existed for `reference/exact-corpus-manifest.json` -- the fifth pin location -- so every bump regenerated its `moduleSha256` column by ad-hoc script, and this one did too. `src/write-corpus-manifest.ts` plus `npm run corpus:manifest` reuses the existing `suiteBrowserModuleDigest`, and encodes the rule the script had to be trusted to follow: the PREVIOUS pin is a required argument, every moved digest must be explained by reverting it, `referenceSha256` refuses rather than adopting new golden bytes, and `capturedAt` is untouched. Proven by reverting the manifest to main's copy and rewriting: byte-identical to the hand-written result, and refusing outright when handed a wrong previous commit

`test/corpus-scenes.test.ts` re-implemented `suiteBrowserModuleDigest` inline over `suiteBrowserModule`, which made the test the only place those digests were computed and would have made the new writer a third copy; the test calls the export now

the writer's guard was proven only by driving the CLI at a wrong previous pin by hand, and its three exports had no importer (`lint:exports` would have flagged all of them). The rule the whole writer rests on is now the pure predicate `moduleMoveExplainedByPin` over the composed TEXT, with a focused test covering the four cases that matter: pin-only churn is explained, a scene that moved beside the pin is not, a wrong previous pin is not, and reverting the commit without the version is not -- that last being the mistake that cost this bump a wrong triage

`TODO.md` grew a second per-release section duplicating the first's heading, preamble and table scaffolding to carry one row, and its preamble spent four of six lines on what is NOT work. Merged into one version-agnostic table with scene 305 as a sixth row

the bump found a failure category the playbook does not list -- a statement ADDED to a body this port restates whole, which every shape and order contract passes -- and every prior bump recorded its own category there. Added as a sixth kind in `docs/development.md`, naming the general fix (pin the statement count) rather than the instance

the same playbook's "Move the pin" table listed four locations where there are five; `reference/exact-corpus-manifest.json` is the one that fails last and reads like a broken bump. Corrected, with the writer and its refusals documented beside it

`assertInventory` is private to `PhysicsLowerer`, so the count guard cannot reach the other lowerers that restate a pinned body whole -- `clustered-light-runtime.ts`'s pinned `_write` (a stride anchor and no body contract), `audio-lowerer.ts` (whose doc claims a body "is exactly these two statements" and checks two presences), `pinned-frame-atlas.ts` and `pinned-grid-atlas.ts`. `assertShapeParamsPrelude` is the same gap one level in: it projects only variable statements, so `_buildShapeParams`' two top-level `if` arms are invisible to it and to `assertShapeParamsCases` alike
findings.blockedBy: generalising needs the helper moved onto `LoweringContext` beside the other shared contract checks, and each body's inventory READ from the pin rather than guessed -- a wrong row refuses on the next bump rather than passing silently, but it still costs that bump. Neither is this bump's diff, and no measurement here covers those four lowerers

findings.summary: `assertPinnedContracts` re-scans havok.ts's 91 top-level statements once per contract, now 13 times per physics compile
findings.blockedBy: measured rather than assumed: `ts.createSourceFile` on the 63,650-byte module is memoized process-wide by `UpstreamSourceStore`, each scan is 1.11 microseconds, and only physics scenes reach the path at all -- roughly 14 microseconds per physics compile, across four scenes in the whole corpus. Below any threshold that would justify restructuring a pre-existing pattern
findings.filedIn: not filed: a measured non-cost, recorded here rather than in TODO.md so it is not re-derived
